{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016dtQ2jsSG9Bi6smNXMyLdt","type":"tool_result","content":"# nurb design doctrine\n\nPrinted via `nurb rules`. This file is the single source; harness files point at it\nrather than repeating it.\n\nThese are standing rules for FDM-printed parts, and several are vetoes rather than\npreferences. Most of them are physics, so they outlive any particular CAD kernel. The\nones that are specific to OCCT are marked as such and were measured, not reasoned.\n\n## The part contract\n\n```python\nfrom nurb import *\n\n@part\ndef dispenser(width=80.0, height=120.0, wall=2.0, draft=False):\n    body = Box(width, height, wall)\n    if draft:\n        return body\n    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed)\n    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n```\n\nKeyword defaults are the parameters. That one declaration feeds the agent, the CLI, the\nviewer, the tests, and any future configurator. Never add a parallel `PARAMS` dict; the\ntwo would drift.\n\n**Write a continuous dimension as a float.** The type of a default is the only thing\nthat says whether a value is a count or a measurement, and the viewer reads it: an `int`\ndefault gets a slider that steps by one, a `float` default one that moves continuously.\n`bracket_count=4` is a count and `chamfer_size=1.0` is a millimetre, so the trailing\n`.0` is doing work. Nothing else has to be declared, and there is no annotation to keep\nin sync, because the type is already there in the signature.\n\n`draft` is optional and injected by the runtime, never passed by a caller. When it is\ntrue, skip the polish pass. It is worth about 20% on a real part, not the 18x a cube\nsuggests.\n\nReturn one solid. A function that returns two loose bodies still reports a plausible\nbounding box and still exports, so nothing downstream catches it.\n\n**When a configuration cannot work, refuse it with `reject`, never a bare raise.** A holder whose hole is narrower than the tool it holds should not build, and `reject(\"drill_hole_width 14 is under the 14.27mm pin vise plus print shrink: raise it above 14.77\", param=\"drill_hole_width\")` is how a part says so. The message states what is wrong and what value fixes it; `param` names the offending parameter so the viewer marks its slider. The viewer presents a refusal as a limit of the design, in amber with the last good geometry still on screen, where a bare `ValueError` arrives as a red traceback that reads as the part being broken. Guard only what would print wrong or not work at all; taste stays a slider.\n\n## Printability\n\n- **Minimum wall 2 to 3mm**, except where fit geometry says otherwise. Fit-critical\n  dimensions are already tuned; do not round them for tidiness.\n- **Print support-free. No floating features.** Parts print bottom down, building up in\n  +z, so every functional feature is grounded. A vertical extrusion or a vertical\n  through hole is self-supporting. A shelf, loop, or band floated partway up with a gap\n  underneath is not.\n- **A counterbore prints mouth toward the bed, and that floats its ceiling.** The shelf the screw head bears on is laid flat over the open pocket, and the smaller hole's first rim is a circle drawn on air; the `hole_ceiling` finding is this exact case, and it appears on any hole rising out of a bridged roof, not just screw pockets. Never answer it with supports inside a pocket nobody can clean: cut the hole with `counterbore(hole_dia, head_dia, head_depth, depth)`, which steps the transition through two sacrificial bridge layers, a slot bridged chord-to-chord across the pocket and the same slot turned ninety degrees across the first, so each layer spans only what the one before it laid and the whole stack prints support-free. Reach for it whenever a design wants a screw head, a nut, or any wider recess on the bed side of a hole.\n- **Corbel rule.** Grounded does not mean a column to the bed. Support-free means no\n  layer overhanging past 45 degrees. Where material would run to the plate only to\n  satisfy printing, carry the feature on a 45 degree underside instead: a short vertical\n  tip of 4 to 6mm below the floor at the front face, then a 45 degree plane falling back\n  into the body. Every layer then overhangs by at most half a bead and bonds to the wall\n  behind it.\n- **Corbels are always exactly 45 degrees**, the same as every other facet. Never\n  steepen one or match it to a ratio. Let the landing point fall where 45 degrees puts\n  it. Mismatched facet angles are a veto: every facet on the part, cosmetic or\n  structural or corbel, has to read as one system.\n- **A large first layer peels its corners as it cools.** Every layer shrinks as it cools and pulls toward the middle of the part, and the pull lands hardest on a sharp plan corner, farthest from the middle and holding on at a point. Past about 20,000mm2 of first layer the accumulated pull beats corner adhesion, and `warp_risk` names the corners that will lift. The fixes are in the outline, which is what makes this a CAD problem where elephant's foot is not: round the vertical corners at 8mm or more, so the peel front is a curve instead of a point, and give a big plate a ribbed floor rather than a solid slab, which is stiffer per gram and halves what contracts. A 1mm polish chamfer is not relief here; it moves the point half a millimetre. The brim and the clean bed are the slicer's share, and they treat the symptom the outline caused. Material multiplies the pull: the threshold is calibrated on PLA, and naming what the machine prints in `printer.toml`, `material = \"abs\"` next to the profile line, tightens it fivefold, because ABS contracts 1 to 2% as it cools where PLA holds under half a percent. PETG judges as PLA, ASA as ABS, and PC and PP tighter still. At the far end the rule stops being about corners: a bed-covering part in ABS, ASA or PC is the wrong material, and the fix is PETG or PLA, not a wider brim.\n- **Elephant's foot is a slicer setting**, not a CAD problem. Do not model around it.\n- **A pin under 5mm across is perimeters with nothing inside.** There is no room between the walls for infill, so a thin printed pin is a tube, loaded in bending at the weakest weld it has, its base. Under 3mm the nozzle is re-melting each ring as it lays the next, and the pin may not survive its own printing. `pin` fires on a free-standing vertical cylinder taller than twice its diameter; a stub or a locating nub has nothing to lever with and stays silent. Reach for the tilt when the whole part fights the bed. An open box printed upright wants support inside; printed flat it has one huge first layer that warps and three finishes that do not match; stood on a corner at 45 degrees, nothing needs support and every face is printed as perimeters, one finish.\n- **Layer bonds are about half strength**, measured near 50% of in-plane tensile for PLA and worse for ASA. A part loaded around a corner, which is every bracket and every L, has no flat orientation that keeps both legs loading in-plane: one of them always pulls its layers apart. Stood at 45 degrees neither does, and the load path never lies in a single weld plane. A tilt moves the weak plane rather than deleting it, so it is not automatic: a hook printed at an angle fails at the same load with the break somewhere else. It earns its keep on corners, not on straight pulls.\n- **`stand(part, tilt, axis, facet)` is the verb.** It rotates the part about a horizontal axis, seats it, and shaves the down corner flat, because a part standing on an unshaved corner meets the bed along a single extrusion line, and that line peels. The facet is 2mm minimum, measured across the flat. 45 degrees is the usual tilt and is not sacred: a shallow part stands at whatever angle brings everything inside the limit. Run the polish pass before standing, in the functional orientation.\n- **Stand a part on the corner that grounds every region, and prefer the lowest stance that does.** For an L that is the outside of its elbow, legs up in a V. The sign of the roll depends on which way the model faces, so check rather than reason: the same L rolled the other way stands on the end of one leg as a chevron, still grounded, still legal, but 60% taller on the same facet, and height on a facet is what spends the adhesion margin. The stance to refuse is the tent, elbow up, one leg's tip hanging in air, and it is easy to miss by eye because nothing about it looks steep: every face of the floating tip can sit at exactly 45 degrees, silent to the overhang rule. The `floating` rule fails any region whose first layer has nothing to sit on and `stability` judges the height, so `nurb check` on the stood variant settles the corner choice. Past grounded, inside the limit, and low, the tilt is taste: what remains is where the facet scar lands, which is the user's call.\n- **A diagonal print is a variant, and it is offered, never imposed.** The facet is cut from visible geometry, and whether that corner may go is not a printability question: only the user knows whether it shows. The pattern is a bool parameter, `diagonal=False`, that applies `stand()` when true, and a card variant that sets it, so it builds, checks against its own baselines, exports its own STL and shows in the viewer like any variant. Give the variant a `note` saying what the tilt buys and costs in plain words, \"prints tilted on a flattened corner: no supports, and stronger across the corner\", never in the doctrine's. Build it speculatively and link it, `?part=x&variant=x_diagonal`; the user judges by looking, and two lines delete it if they pass.\n- **Past about twenty times the facet width in height, adhesion is holding a lever, and `stand()` grows fins.** A compact part holds its facet by first-layer adhesion; a tall one needs support fins modelled into the part, never slicer supports, whose loose grip lets warp tension spring the part free mid-print. The recipe is print-farm practice with fixed numbers, so it is generated rather than judged: a thin blade at each side of the part hugging the lean across a small gap, each on a 1mm pad for its own adhesion, joined to the part only by horizontal tines a single layer tall and a bead wide, about 0.5 x 0.5mm, five or so, biased toward the bottom where the young print is least stable. After printing the fins lift off whole and the tine stubs rub off with a fingernail. The tines cost a handful of sub-millimetre faces, declared on the card like any other earned sliver. The stability warning remains the referee for what `stand()` did not build: pass `fins=False` to see it, and a part tilted by hand still gets it.\n\n## Load path\n\nWork out where the weight sits and what it does at the mount before drawing anything.\n\n- **Shear**, a straight down load close to the wall, is handled well and rarely needs\n  reinforcement.\n- **Bending moment**, a load projecting forward, is the dominant failure mode. Load\n  times distance levers the top of the part off its mount and concentrates stress at\n  the inside corner where the platform meets the body.\n- **Lateral load and torsion** are answered by a second mount point, not by thickening.\n  A single-mount part carrying an off-center load twists.\n- **FDM is anisotropic.** Layer bonds are the weak direction and a cantilever moment\n  peels them apart. Spread load into the body with gussets rather than adding section\n  thickness.\n\n**Projection-to-height ratio** decides the reinforcement. A loaded shelf pries at the\nwall as a force couple, and those forces scale with projection divided by the height of\nthe supporting back. Doubling the height halves the pull-out force, and height in the\nwall plane is nearly free: no forward mass, almost no material.\n\n```\n<= 1.5x    chamfers only\n1.5 - 2.5x end gussets\n> 2.5x     raise the height until it is back under 2.5, then gussets\n```\n\nDo not oversize either. A light part sits near the mounting system's minimum height. An\noversized back on a small hook is wasted material and looks wrong. `nurb check` reports\nthis ratio for any part whose card names which way it reaches.\n\n### Reinforcement, in order of preference\n\n1. **Gussets**, triangular webs joining the platform top to the body front. The most\n   effective cantilever fix, because they turn bending into compression along the\n   diagonal. Depth about half the projection, height as tall as the body allows while\n   staying low. **Outer ends only, never mid-surface**: a mid-surface gusset obstructs\n   the usable area.\n2. **Inside-corner relief**, 3mm, at every load-bearing junction. Cheap, always worth it.\n3. **Ribs** under a large platform to stop plate flex, 2 to 3mm wide, front to back.\n4. **Another mount point.** When in doubt, add one. The wall interface is stronger than\n   the printed part.\n\n**Gussets are truncated quadrilaterals, never sharp triangles.** End the outer tip with\na short vertical face of about 6mm, drawn in the profile. A part gets looked at every day it hangs on the wall, and among the shapes that all work, pick the one worth looking at. The priority is fixed: a measured fit is never rounded for looks and structure is never thinned for elegance. A uniform slab reads as unconsidered; a gusseted, relieved shape explains itself.\n- **Symmetry is the default.** An asymmetric feature is earned by function, a cable exit, a handed mount, and once earned it is committed to rather than half-hidden.\n- **Features align.** Holes share a centerline, faces land on shared planes, repeated features sit on an even rhythm. An edge that almost lines up with another is worse than either placement.\n- **Restraint is the ornament.** The faceted language, one chamfer size, every facet at 45 degrees, is already the decoration. Nothing decorative gets added that printability has to pay for, and nothing arbitrary breaks the system.\n\nBeyond these, proportion is taste, and taste is a slider: expose the parameter and let the user's eye decide in the viewer rather than defending a number in chat.\n\n## Polish pass\n\nThe polish pass runs last, after structure is finished.\n\n1. **Chamfers are the default on exposed edges**, 1mm, never below 0.8mm. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d0182a6b-03a3-4a18-8f8f-79eb2109cd0a","uuid":"41d7dcf8-ffec-4793-a1db-ece95a1c5fc3","timestamp":"2026-08-24T00:31:12.546Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/private/var/folders/s4/by90nw7j7_l_nvvqs3hd9mjh0000gn/T/nurb-eval-trial-1_put0yb/project/parts/pole_rest.py","oldString":"    wall=1.8,","newString":"    wall=2.5,","originalFile":"from nurb import *\n\n\n@part\ndef pole_rest(\n    pole_diameter=20.0,\n    length=22.0,\n    clearance=0.2,\n    wall=1.8,\n    margin=2.0,\n    draft=False,\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n    axis_height = 18.0\n\n    if clearance < 0.1:\n        reject(\n            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n            param=\"clearance\",\n        )\n\n    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n\n    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n    width = 2 * half_width\n\n    # Block runs from the bed up to the pole's centre height: subtracting the\n    # cradle cylinder there carves a true half-cylinder groove (180 degrees),\n    # open straight upward, so the pole drops straight in from above.\n    body = Box(width, length, axis_height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n    groove = Cylinder(inner_radius, length + 2, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    groove = groove.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n\n    body = body - groove\n\n    if draft:\n        return body\n\n    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":6,"oldLines":7,"newStart":6,"newLines":7,"lines":["     pole_diameter=20.0,","     length=22.0,","     clearance=0.2,","-    wall=1.8,","+    wall=2.5,","     margin=2.0,","     draft=False,"," ):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HtFNcHARxZMpzkYs1yaRYb","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tfrom nurb import *\n2\t\n3\t\n4\t@part\n5\tdef pole_rest(\n6\t    pole_diameter=20.0,\n7\t    length=22.0,\n8\t    clearance=0.2,\n9\t    wall=2.5,\n10\t    margin=2.0,\n11\t    draft=False,\n12\t):\n13\t    \"\"\"\n14\t    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n15\t    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n16\t    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n17\t    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n18\t    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n19\t    \"\"\"\n20\t    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n21\t    axis_height = 18.0\n22\t\n23\t    if clearance < 0.1:\n24\t        reject(\n25\t            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n26\t            param=\"clearance\",\n27\t        )\n28\t\n29\t    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n30\t    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n31\t\n32\t    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n33\t    width = 2 * half_width\n34\t\n35\t    # Stop the block a hair below the pole's centre height: subtracting the\n36\t    # cradle cylinder there carves a wide (just under 180 degree) groove that\n37\t    # meets the flat top at a real angle rather than a zero-thickness tangent,\n38\t    # and still opens straight upward so the pole drops in from above.\n39\t    lip = 2.0\n40\t    top_z = axis_height - lip\n41\t    body = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n42\t    groove = Cylinder(inner_radius, length + 20, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n43\t    groove = groove.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n44\t\n45\t    body = body - groove\n46\t\n47\t    if draft:\n48\t        return body\n49\t\n50\t    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n51\t    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n52\t    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n53\t    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n54\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d0182a6b-03a3-4a18-8f8f-79eb2109cd0a","uuid":"73f91685-9feb-4809-890b-bcaff52620b4","timestamp":"2026-08-24T00:35:53.854Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/private/var/folders/s4/by90nw7j7_l_nvvqs3hd9mjh0000gn/T/nurb-eval-trial-1_put0yb/project/parts/pole_rest.py","content":"from nurb import *\n\n\n@part\ndef pole_rest(\n    pole_diameter=20.0,\n    length=22.0,\n    clearance=0.2,\n    wall=2.5,\n    margin=2.0,\n    draft=False,\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n    axis_height = 18.0\n\n    if clearance < 0.1:\n        reject(\n            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n            param=\"clearance\",\n        )\n\n    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n\n    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n    width = 2 * half_width\n\n    # Stop the block a hair below the pole's centre height: subtracting the\n    # cradle cylinder there carves a wide (just under 180 degree) groove that\n    # meets the flat top at a real angle rather than a zero-thickness tangent,\n    # and still opens straight upward so the pole drops in from above.\n    lip = 2.0\n    top_z = axis_height - lip\n    body = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n    groove = Cylinder(inner_radius, length + 20, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    groove = groove.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n\n    body = body - groove\n\n    if draft:\n        return body\n\n    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n","numLines":54,"startLine":1,"totalLines":54}}}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d0182a6b-03a3-4a18-8f8f-79eb2109cd0a","uuid":"a1af1043-a2ce-4a9f-99f8-e8a7dc4abf8c","timestamp":"2026-08-24T00:38:32.372Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/private/var/folders/s4/by90nw7j7_l_nvvqs3hd9mjh0000gn/T/nurb-eval-trial-1_put0yb/project/parts/pole_rest.py","oldString":"    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 0.5","newString":"    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 2.5","originalFile":"from nurb import *\n\n\n@part\ndef pole_rest(\n    pole_diameter=20.0,\n    length=22.0,\n    clearance=0.2,\n    wall=2.5,\n    margin=2.0,\n    draft=False,\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n    axis_height = 18.0\n\n    if clearance < 0.1:\n        reject(\n            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n            param=\"clearance\",\n        )\n\n    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n\n    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n    width = 2 * half_width\n\n    # Stop the groove a hair below the pole's centre height so it opens just\n    # under 180 degrees, straight upward, letting the pole drop in from above.\n    lip = 0.6\n    top_z = axis_height - lip\n\n    # The cradle is a constant-thickness pipe (outer cylinder minus inner\n    # cylinder), never a box cut by a circle: a box's flat side meeting a\n    # circle tangent to it pinches the material to zero width right at the\n    # bottom of the arc. The pipe keeps `wall` of material everywhere along\n    # the arc instead, and a flat slab under it, reaching only up to the\n    # pipe's own lowest point, gives it a bed footprint without reintroducing\n    # that pinch (both pieces are solid there, so the seam is never thin).\n    span = length + 20\n    outer_cyl = Cylinder(outer_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    inner_cyl = Cylinder(inner_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    pipe = outer_cyl - inner_cyl\n    pipe = pipe.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n\n    bounds = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n    pipe = pipe & bounds\n\n    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 0.5\n    base = Box(width, length, base_height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n\n    body = pipe + base\n\n    if draft:\n        return body\n\n    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":53,"oldLines":7,"newStart":53,"newLines":7,"lines":["     bounds = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))","     pipe = pipe & bounds"," ","-    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 0.5","+    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 2.5","     base = Box(width, length, base_height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))"," ","     body = pipe + base"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01ViLe2bACBWG5N6hz5WeoU1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tfrom nurb import *\n2\t\n3\t\n4\t@part\n5\tdef pole_rest(\n6\t    pole_diameter=20.0,\n7\t    length=22.0,\n8\t    clearance=0.2,\n9\t    wall=2.5,\n10\t    margin=2.0,\n11\t    draft=False,\n12\t):\n13\t    \"\"\"\n14\t    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n15\t    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n16\t    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n17\t    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n18\t    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n19\t    \"\"\"\n20\t    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n21\t    axis_height = 18.0\n22\t\n23\t    if clearance < 0.1:\n24\t        reject(\n25\t            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n26\t            param=\"clearance\",\n27\t        )\n28\t\n29\t    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n30\t    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n31\t\n32\t    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n33\t    width = 2 * half_width\n34\t\n35\t    # Stop the groove a hair below the pole's centre height so it opens just\n36\t    # under 180 degrees, straight upward, letting the pole drop in from above.\n37\t    lip = 3.0\n38\t    top_z = axis_height - lip\n39\t\n40\t    # The cradle is a constant-thickness pipe (outer cylinder minus inner\n41\t    # cylinder), never a box cut by a circle: a box's flat side meeting a\n42\t    # circle tangent to it pinches the material to zero width right at the\n43\t    # bottom of the arc. The pipe keeps `wall` of material everywhere along\n44\t    # the arc instead, and a flat slab under it, reaching only up to the\n45\t    # pipe's own lowest point, gives it a bed footprint without reintroducing\n46\t    # that pinch (both pieces are solid there, so the seam is never thin).\n47\t    span = length + 20\n48\t    outer_cyl = Cylinder(outer_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n49\t    inner_cyl = Cylinder(inner_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n50\t    pipe = outer_cyl - inner_cyl\n51\t    pipe = pipe.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n52\t\n53\t    bounds = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n54\t    pipe = pipe & bounds\n55\t\n56\t    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 2.5\n57\t    base = Box(width, length, base_height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n58\t\n59\t    body = pipe + base\n60\t\n61\t    if draft:\n62\t        return body\n63\t\n64\t    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n65\t    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n66\t    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n67\t    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n68\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d0182a6b-03a3-4a18-8f8f-79eb2109cd0a","uuid":"44b92629-a49c-4309-8afd-856af92030f5","timestamp":"2026-08-24T00:40:48.080Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/private/var/folders/s4/by90nw7j7_l_nvvqs3hd9mjh0000gn/T/nurb-eval-trial-1_put0yb/project/parts/pole_rest.py","content":"from nurb import *\n\n\n@part\ndef pole_rest(\n    pole_diameter=20.0,\n    length=22.0,\n    clearance=0.2,\n    wall=2.5,\n    margin=2.0,\n    draft=False,\n):\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_diameter: diameter of the pole this rest cradles\n    length: how long the rest runs along the pole's axis\n    clearance: gap between the cradle and the pole's surface\n    wall: material thickness behind the cradle surface\n    margin: extra material at the base beyond the cradle's footprint\n    \"\"\"\n    pole_radius = pole_diameter / 2.0\n    axis_height = 18.0\n\n    if clearance < 0.1:\n        reject(\n            f\"clearance {clearance} is under the 0.1mm minimum stand-off from the pole\",\n            param=\"clearance\",\n        )\n\n    inner_radius = pole_radius + clearance\n    outer_radius = inner_radius + wall + 1.2\n\n    half_width = outer_radius + margin\n    width = 2 * half_width\n\n    # Stop the groove a hair below the pole's centre height so it opens just\n    # under 180 degrees, straight upward, letting the pole drop in from above.\n    lip = 3.0\n    top_z = axis_height - lip\n\n    # The cradle is a constant-thickness pipe (outer cylinder minus inner\n    # cylinder), never a box cut by a circle: a box's flat side meeting a\n    # circle tangent to it pinches the material to zero width right at the\n    # bottom of the arc. The pipe keeps `wall` of material everywhere along\n    # the arc instead, and a flat slab under it, reaching only up to the\n    # pipe's own lowest point, gives it a bed footprint without reintroducing\n    # that pinch (both pieces are solid there, so the seam is never thin).\n    span = length + 20\n    outer_cyl = Cylinder(outer_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    inner_cyl = Cylinder(inner_radius, span, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER))\n    pipe = outer_cyl - inner_cyl\n    pipe = pipe.rotate(Axis.X, 90).locate(Location((0, 0, axis_height)))\n\n    bounds = Box(width, length, top_z, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n    pipe = pipe & bounds\n\n    base_height = axis_height - outer_radius + 2.5\n    base = Box(width, length, base_height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))\n\n    body = pipe + base\n\n    if draft:\n        return body\n\n    bed = body.bounding_box().min.Z\n    cradle = concave_edges(body)\n    keep = body.edges().filter_by(lambda e: e.bounding_box().min.Z > bed) - cradle\n    return polish(body, keep, 1.0)\n","numLines":68,"startLine":1,"totalLines":68}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CeLeJCWoNHhpTDApiDeev","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01AMYqVxFyCYK1bnZoaNVXek","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/private/var/folders/s4/by90nw7j7_l_nvvqs3hd9mjh0000gn/T/nurb-eval-trial-1_put0yb/project/parts/pole_rest.md","old_string":"## What it is\n\n## Design notes\n\n## Don't\n\n## Changelog","new_string":"## What it is\n\nA bench-top cradle for a freshly finished pole while it dries. Several stand\nin a row; the pole lies across them along Y with its axis fixed at 18.0mm\nabove the bed, centered over the part's footprint in X. The cradle is a\nconstant-thickness half-pipe (a wide, near-180-degree arc) so the soft\nfinish is supported on a curve, not balanced on an edge or a point.\n\n## Design notes\n\n- The cradle is built as an annulus (`outer cylinder - inner cylinder`),\n  never as a box with a cylinder subtracted from it. A flat block cut by a\n  tangent circle pinches to zero material thickness right at the bottom of\n  the arc, which `nurb check`'s `min_wall` catches; the pipe keeps `wall` of\n  material behind the pole everywhere along the arc instead.\n- `lip` (currently 3.0mm, hardcoded) stops the groove that far below the\n  pole's centre height. This keeps the arc's open mouth away from the\n  tangent zone at the very top of the circle, where the flat lid and the\n  bore would otherwise meet edge-on and print a knife edge. It also keeps\n  the arc under 180 degrees so the pole can drop straight down into the\n  seat without the walls overhanging past vertical.\n- `clearance` (default 0.2mm) is the standoff from the pole's surface; below\n  0.1mm the part refuses to build via `reject`.\n- `wall` (default 2.5mm) plus a fixed 1.2mm is the radial thickness of the\n  pipe, well past the printer's minimum wall and the checker's backing\n  requirement.\n\n## Don't\n\n- Don't cut the groove from a solid box with a single cylinder subtraction.\n  It looks simpler but pinches to a knife edge at the bottom of the arc —\n  see Design notes.\n- Don't shrink `lip` toward 0.
